lab_title: Unlocking Retrograde Motion: From Geocentric Puzzle to Heliocentric Reality
top_level_objectives: Identify the characteristics of apparent retrograde motion from an Earth-bound perspective.
Distinguish between geocentric observations and heliocentric orbital reality.
Explain retrograde motion as a result of relative orbital speeds between Earth and outer planets.
Compare how the distance of an outer planet from the Sun influences the retrograde loop.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the student to the phenomenon of retrograde motion from an Earth-bound perspective.
key_visuals: A night sky dome featuring a constellation backdrop.
A glowing trail marking Mars's position over several weeks.
student_actions: Use a slider to scrub through time, observing Mars tracing its path across the sky.
Note where Mars slows down, reverses, and then resumes its eastward drift.

scenes.brief_purpose: Visualize the solar system from a top-down, heliocentric perspective to contrast with the Earthbound view.
key_visuals: A 3D model of the inner solar system (Sun, Earth, Mars).
student_actions: Toggle between Earth's view and a 'God's eye' view of the solar system.
Observe the planets orbiting the Sun at different speeds.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how the overtaking maneuver creates the illusion of backward motion.
key_visuals: An augmented overlay connecting the Earth, Mars, and the background stars.
A visual projection showing the line-of-sight path from Earth to Mars.
student_actions: Sync the orbital motions of Earth and Mars.
Observe the 'line of sight' changing as Earth passes Mars, creating the retrograde loop on the celestial sphere.

scenes.brief_purpose: Deepen the understanding by using the 'passing car' analogy.
key_visuals: Two cars moving on parallel roads on a 3D grid.
A visual indicator of the relative speed between the vehicles.
student_actions: Control the speed of the 'Earth car' as it passes the 'Mars car'.
Observe how the background scenery shifts differently based on the observer's relative speed.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate that retrograde motion is a universal effect for outer planets.
key_visuals: A wider view of the solar system including Jupiter and Saturn.
Multiple retrograde loops appearing on a dashboard display.
student_actions: Select different outer planets (Jupiter, Saturn) to compare the size and frequency of their retrograde loops.
Observe why the retrograde loops of more distant planets are less pronounced.

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate learning by asking students to predict outcomes.
student_actions: Position Earth and Mars to create a retrograde event.
Sketch or mark the predicted path of Mars on the sky-dome based on the planetary alignment.
